backlog.title: Implement the spec refinements from commit 0ea555ed
backlog.description: Three REQUIRED feature groups from the spec delta, none of which are implemented today: G3 marker retraction (cancel), G2 stale-marker retirement + soft cap, G1 drift-nudge refinements (windowed signaling + high-water signal). All reuse existing shipped patterns — no new architecture, no new event, no new model request (D4 holds). Build order: M1 (cancel primitive) → M2 (stale retirement reuses cancel) → M3 (independent drift refinements) → M4 (doc sync).

milestones.title: Marker retraction (G3; amends D6)
milestones.description: An agent can cancel any mulligan:rewind/mulligan:shrink marker by id; on the next context fire the cancelled transform no longer applies; mulligan_audit lists cancelled markers as retired; cancelling a non-existent/already-cancelled id is a safe no-op that never throws. Acceptance criteria a–d in spec/08 E21.

tasks.title: Cancel marker data model & persistence wrapper (markers.ts)
tasks.description: Add the CancelMarker envelope shape, extend MulliganEnvelope.kind, and add the appendCancelMarker wrapper mirroring the existing appendShrinkMarker pattern.

subtasks.title: CancelMarker interface + MulliganEnvelope.kind extension + appendCancelMarker wrapper
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: See plan/003_2c3b19ff6a7b/architecture/system_context.md (markers.ts current state) and implementation_patterns.md §Pattern 1. The existing appendShrinkMarker(pi, ctx, data) in src/markers.ts is the EXACT template — it stamps {schema:'pi-mulligan', v:1, kind, seq, ts}, calls pi.appendEntry('mulligan:shrink', entry), returns ctx.sessionManager.getLeafId(), never throws. MulliganEnvelope.kind is currently "rewind" | "shrink" | "turn-metric".
2. INPUT: No runtime input — this is a foundational data model change. Uses nextSeq(sessionId) from runtime.ts, randomUUID from node:crypto, pi.appendEntry + ctx.sessionManager.getLeafId/getSessionId (identical to appendShrinkMarker).
3. LOGIC: (a) Extend MulliganEnvelope.kind to "rewind" | "shrink" | "turn-metric" | "cancel" (closed union stays closed). (b) Add interface CancelMarker extends MulliganEnvelope { kind: "cancel"; targetId: string; seq: number; ts: number }. The targetId is the uuid `id` field of the rewind/shrink marker being cancelled. CancelMarker does NOT have its own `id` uuid field (like TurnMetric — it is not itself cancellable). (c) Add type CancelMarkerInput = Omit<CancelMarker, "schema" | "v" | "kind" | "seq" | "ts"> — i.e. just { targetId: string }. (d) Add appendCancelMarker(pi: ExtensionAPI, ctx: ExtensionContext, data: CancelMarkerInput): string | null — mirror appendShrinkMarker EXACTLY: const sessionId = ctx.sessionManager.getSessionId(); const seq = nextSeq(sessionId); const entry = { ...data, schema:'pi-mulligan', v:1, kind:'cancel', seq, ts: Date.now() }; pi.appendEntry('mulligan:cancel', entry); return ctx.sessionManager.getLeafId(); — wrapped in try/catch → return null (never throws, per fail-open discipline E13).
4. OUTPUT: Exports CancelMarker, CancelMarkerInput, appendCancelMarker. Consumed by filter.ts readMarkers (P3.M1.T2.S1), tools/cancel.ts (P3.M1.T3.S1), filter.ts stale-retirement (P3.M2.T3.S1), and audit.ts (P3.M1.T4.S1).
5. MOCKING: In tests, reuse the makePi()/makeCtx() fakes from test/markers.test.ts (capture appendEntry calls, script getLeafId). Assert: appendCancelMarker calls pi.appendEntry('mulligan:cancel', {schema, v:1, kind:'cancel', targetId, seq, ts}) and returns the scripted leaf id. Assert it returns null and never throws when appendEntry/getLeafId/getSessionId throws.
6. DOCS: [Mode A] Add the CancelMarker shape to spec/04-data-model.md — a new subsection after §5 (Turn metric), documenting {kind:"cancel", targetId, seq, ts} and that it carries no `id` field (like turn-metric). This rides WITH the work.

tasks.title: readMarkers cancel-drop + MarkersBundle extension (filter.ts)
tasks.description: Extend readMarkers to collect mulligan:cancel entries, build a cancelledIds set, drop cancelled rewinds/shrinks before returning, and expose cancelledIds on MarkersBundle.

subtasks.title: Collect cancel entries, build cancelledIds, drop cancelled markers, expose on MarkersBundle
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: See plan/003_2c3b19ff6a7b/architecture/implementation_patterns.md §Pattern 2. The current readMarkers(ctx) in src/filter.ts scans type==='custom' entries, dispatches on customType+kind, pushes rewinds/shrinks, keeps latest metric. RewindMarker and ShrinkMarker both have an `id` field (uuid stamped by appendRewindMarker/appendShrinkMarker). CancelMarker (from P3.M1.T1.S1) has customType 'mulligan:cancel', kind 'cancel', and a `targetId` field referencing the marker's uuid `id`.
2. INPUT: The CancelMarker interface and 'mulligan:cancel' customType from P3.M1.T1.S1. The existing readMarkers entry-scan loop in src/filter.ts (lines ~115-145).
3. LOGIC: (a) In the readMarkers loop, add an else-if branch: if customType==='mulligan:cancel' && kind==='cancel', read targetId via readOwn(data, 'targetId'); if it's a non-empty string, add to a new Set<string> cancelledIds. (b) After the loop, filter rewinds and shrinks to drop any whose `id` field ∈ cancelledIds: const activeRewinds = rewinds.filter(r => { const id = readOwn(r, 'id'); return typeof id !== 'string' || !cancelledIds.has(id); }) — same for shrinks. (c) Extend MarkersBundle interface to add cancelledIds: Set<string>. (d) Return { rewinds: activeRewinds, shrinks: activeShrinks, metric, cancelledIds }. Cancelled markers stay on disk (audit trail) — they are just skipped going forward. NEVER throws (existing defensive readOwn/isRecord pattern continues).
4. OUTPUT: MarkersBundle now has cancelledIds. Consumed by contextHandler (the pipeline only sees active markers), audit.ts renderAuditReport (P3.M1.T4.S1 lists cancelled count), and the stale-retirement logic (P3.M2.T3.S1).
5. MOCKING: In tests, build fake session entries with makeCancelEntry(targetId) alongside existing rewindData/shrinkData/customEntry helpers from test/filter.test.ts. Assert: cancelling a shrink → the shrink is absent from readMarkers().shrinks; cancelling a rewind → absent from rewinds; cancelling a non-existent id → no markers dropped; multiple cancels → all targeted markers dropped; cancelledIds set contains the right ids.
6. DOCS: [Mode A] Document the cancel-drop in spec/06-context-filter.md §1 (readMarkers) — add a note that readMarkers also collects mulligan:cancel entries and drops any marker whose id is cancelled before returning the bundle. This rides WITH the work.

tasks.title: mulligan_cancel tool (tools/cancel.ts + index.ts registration)
tasks.description: Create the mulligan_cancel agent-callable tool following the makeShrinkTool(pi) factory pattern. Takes a markerId (the entry id from details.markerId), validates, appends a cancel marker, returns confirmation. Safe no-op for non-existent/already-cancelled. Never throws.

subtasks.title: Create mulligan_cancel tool + register in index.ts
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: See plan/003_2c3b19ff6a7b/architecture/implementation_patterns.md §Pattern 3 and system_context.md §tools/shrink.ts. The makeShrinkTool(pi) factory in src/tools/shrink.ts is the EXACT template: defineTool({name, label, description, parameters, async execute(toolCallId, params, signal, onUpdate, ctx) {...}}), with pi captured via closure. Every return path includes a `details` field (required by Pi type). refusal(reason) returns {content:[{type:'text',text:'Mulligan: refused — <reason>.'}], details:{}}. The whole execute body is ONE try/catch → refusal text on any exception (E13). The agent receives the cancel target as `markerId` — the ENTRY id returned in details.markerId by mulligan_rewind/mulligan_shrink (which is getLeafId()).
2. INPUT: appendCancelMarker(pi, ctx, {targetId}) from P3.M1.T1.S1. The readMarkers cancel-drop from P3.M1.T2.S1 ensures the cancel takes effect next fire. getConfig() from src/config.ts. ctx.sessionManager.getEntries() from Pi (read FRESH — C12).
3. LOGIC: (a) Create src/tools/cancel.ts. (b) CancelParams = Type.Object({ markerId: Type.String({ description: 'The marker id to cancel (the markerId value returned by mulligan_rewind or mulligan_shrink in details.markerId).' }) }). (c) CancelDetails = { cancelled: boolean; markerId?: string | null; reason?: string }. (d) makeCancelTool(pi): ToolDefinition<typeof CancelParams, CancelDetails> — factory captures pi. (e) execute body: 1. config gate — if !getConfig().enabled, return refusal('Mulligan is disabled') (E14). 2. Scan ctx.sessionManager.getEntries() for a custom entry whose entry.id === params.markerId AND customType ∈ {'mulligan:rewind', 'mulligan:shrink'}. 3. If not found → safe no-op: return {content:[{type:'text', text:'Mulligan: no active marker found with that id — nothing to cancel.'}], details:{cancelled:false}}. 4. Read the marker's uuid id from entry.data.id (via readOwn). 5. Scan entries for an existing mulligan:cancel with data.targetId === uuid → if found, safe no-op: return {content:[{type:'text', text:'Mulligan: that marker is already cancelled.'}], details:{cancelled:false}}. 6. appendCancelMarker(pi, ctx, {targetId: uuid}) → markerId (entry id or null). 7. Return {content:[{type:'text', text:'Mulligan: marker cancelled. The transform will no longer apply from the next turn on.'}], details:{cancelled:true, markerId}}. (f) WRAP the entire body in ONE try/catch → refusal('unexpected error: <msg>') (E13). (g) Register in src/index.ts: add `import { makeCancelTool } from './tools/cancel.js'` and `pi.registerTool(makeCancelTool(pi))` alongside the existing tool registrations.
4. OUTPUT: Exports makeCancelTool, CancelParams, CancelDetails, CANCEL_DESC. index.ts now registers the 5th tool.
5. MOCKING: In tests, reuse the makePi()/makeCtx() fakes (script getEntries to return custom entries with entry.id, customType, data.id). Assert: cancelling an existing rewind → appendCancelMarker called with the right targetId + confirmation text; cancelling a shrink → same; non-existent markerId → no-op text + details.cancelled===false; already-cancelled → no-op text; config.enabled===false → refusal text; appendEntry throws → refusal text (never throws).
6. DOCS: [Mode A] Add a mulligan_cancel tool entry to spec/05-tools.md (new §3.5 or renumber): parameter schema (markerId string), return shape, behavior (step by step mirroring §2 mulligan_shrink), refusal conditions (disabled, non-existent, already-cancelled). Reference the D6-amendment framing from SPEC.md. This rides WITH the work.

milestones.title: Stale-marker retirement + soft cap (G2; depends on P3.M1)
milestones.description: Bound long-session filter cost per spec/08 E15. A pinned shrink whose target entry has been absent for config.shrink.staleAfterFires (default 3) consecutive fires is auto-retired; active shrink markers are capped at config.shrink.maxActive (default 32), oldest retired when exceeded. Retirement reuses the G3 cancel primitive (appendCancelMarker).

tasks.title: Config knobs: shrink.maxActive + shrink.staleAfterFires (config.ts)
tasks.description: Add two numeric knobs to the shrink config block using the established coerceNumber pattern.

subtasks.title: Add shrink.maxActive (32) and shrink.staleAfterFires (3) to MulliganConfig, DEFAULT_CONFIG, validateConfig
subtasks.context_scope:

The MulliganConfig.shrink block currently has only { enabled: boolean }. The established pattern for numeric knobs: coerceNumber(field, value, fallback, mustBePositive) — finite number >0, else warn + fallback. validateConfig's shrink block reads via safeGet(shrinkRaw, key) and coerces. Both mustBePositive=true (>0). (d) NOTE: the reserved autoOnBloat stays OUT (spec/07 D3 — not v1).

tasks.title: Stale retirement + soft cap logic (filter.ts contextHandler)
tasks.description: After filterPipeline runs, walk active pinned shrinks to track hit/miss counts and auto-retire stale ones; separately cap active shrinks at maxActive. Both reuse appendCancelMarker from P3.M1. This requires threading pi into contextHandler.

subtasks.title: Thread pi into contextHandler + stale-marker retirement logic
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: See plan/003_2c3b19ff6a7b/architecture/implementation_patterns.md §Pattern 7 (GOTCHA — pi in contextHandler). contextHandler(event, ctx) currently does NOT receive pi. registerFilterHandler(pi) does pi.on('context', contextHandler). To call appendCancelMarker(pi, ctx, ...) inside contextHandler, change the signature: registerFilterHandler wraps the handler — pi.on('context', (event, ctx) => contextHandler(pi, event, ctx)) — and contextHandler becomes (pi, event, ctx). This mirrors the turnEndMetricHandler(pi, event, ctx) pattern in nudges.ts. resolvePinnedShrink(messages, branchEntries, pinnedEntryId) is already exported from transforms.ts (Pi-free) and can be called from filter.ts to check if a pinned shrink's target is present. NOTE: this subtask touches the SAME contextHandler function that P3.M1.T2.S1 may have modified (readMarkers changes) — build on top of it.
2. INPUT: appendCancelMarker(pi, ctx, {targetId}) from P3.M1.T1.S1. config.shrink.staleAfterFires from P3.M2.T1.S1. rt.shrinkMissCounts from P3.M2.T2.S1. markers.shrinks (the ACTIVE shrinks after cancel-drop from P3.M1.T2.S1) from readMarkers. resolvePinnedShrink from transforms.ts. event.messages (pre-filterPipeline) + branchEntries for the resolution pass.
3. LOGIC: (a) Change contextHandler signature to (pi: ExtensionAPI, event: ContextEvent, ctx: ExtensionContext). (b) Change registerFilterHandler to: pi.on('context', (event, ctx) => contextHandler(pi, event, ctx)). (c) AFTER filterPipeline runs (on the filtered messages) and BEFORE the return, add the stale-retirement pass: for each active shrink in markers.shrinks that has a pinnedEntryId (read via readOwn), call resolvePinnedShrink(event.messages, branchEntries, pinnedEntryId) to check if the target is present. If present (non-null) → rt.shrinkMissCounts.set(shrink.id, 0) (reset). If absent (null) → rt.shrinkMissCounts.set(shrink.id, (rt.shrinkMissCounts.get(shrink.id) ?? 0) + 1). If the count reaches config.shrink.staleAfterFires → appendCancelMarker(pi, ctx, { targetId: shrink.id }) (auto-retire). (d) This append takes effect on the NEXT fire (readMarkers drops the cancelled id) — no in-fire mutation. (e) NEVER throws: wrap the stale-retirement pass in its own try/catch inside the outer try/catch (a failure in retirement must not break the turn — E13). (f) Only process shrinks with pinnedEntryId (live shrinks cannot go stale — they re-resolve each fire and either match or no-op harmlessly).
4. OUTPUT: contextHandler now accepts pi and performs stale retirement. Pinned shrinks whose target has been absent for staleAfterFires consecutive fires are auto-retired (a mulligan:cancel is appended). registerFilterHandler wires pi through.
5. MOCKING: In tests, script a fake session with a pinned shrink whose target entry is ABSENT from branchEntries. Fire contextHandler multiple times — assert that after staleAfterFires fires, appendCancelMarker was called (pi.appendEntry called with 'mulligan:cancel'). Assert that a pinned shrink whose target IS present does NOT get retired (miss count stays 0). Assert rt.shrinkMissCounts resets on hit. Assert the turn never breaks even if resolvePinnedShrink throws.
6. DOCS: none — the stale-retirement behavior is already specified in spec/08 E15 (the source of this delta). No additional Mode A docs needed.

subtasks.title: Soft cap: retire oldest shrink when active count exceeds maxActive
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: See plan/003_2c3b19ff6a7b/architecture/implementation_patterns.md §Pattern 7 (cap logic). After P3.M2.T3.S1, contextHandler already has pi threaded in and runs the stale-retirement pass. The soft cap is a SEPARATE check in the same post-filterPipeline block. Active shrinks = markers.shrinks (already cancel-dropped by readMarkers). The 'oldest' shrink is the one with the lowest seq.
2. INPUT: config.shrink.maxActive from P3.M2.T1.S1. markers.shrinks (active shrinks, already cancel-dropped). appendCancelMarker(pi, ctx, {targetId}) from P3.M1.T1.S1. pi is now available in contextHandler (from P3.M2.T3.S1).
3. LOGIC: After the stale-retirement pass (from P3.M2.T3.S1), add: if markers.shrinks.length > config.shrink.maxActive, find the oldest shrink by seq (sort ascending, take first), and call appendCancelMarker(pi, ctx, { targetId: oldest.id }). This retires exactly ONE shrink per fire (the oldest) — if the cap is exceeded by N, it takes N fires to bring it under the cap, which is acceptable (bounded, eventual). Wrap in the same try/catch as the stale pass (never breaks the turn). Do NOT retire more than one per fire (keeps the logic simple and the cost bounded).
4. OUTPUT: Active shrink markers are capped at config.shrink.maxActive. When exceeded, the oldest is retired on the next fire.
5. MOCKING: In tests, script a session with maxActive=2 and 3 active shrinks. Fire contextHandler — assert appendCancelMarker was called with the targetId of the shrink with the lowest seq. Assert only ONE cancel is appended per fire.
6. DOCS: none — the soft-cap behavior is already specified in spec/08 E15 + spec/09 (the source of this delta).

milestones.title: Drift-nudge refinements (G1; windowed signaling + high-water)
milestones.description: Cut drift-nudge false positives (§5.1 windowed signaling) and catch slow accumulation (§5.2 edge-triggered high-water signal). Both ride the existing context event (D4 — zero extra requests). Per spec/07 §5.1/§5.2 and spec/09.

tasks.title: Config knobs + threshold raise (config.ts)
tasks.description: Add nudges.driftWindowTurns (3), nudges.highWaterFraction (0.7), and raise nudges.driftThresholdTokens from 3000 to 6000.

subtasks.title: Add driftWindowTurns, highWaterFraction; raise driftThresholdTokens 3000→6000
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: See plan/003_2c3b19ff6a7b/architecture/system_context.md §config.ts and external_deps.md (config validation pattern). DEFAULT_CONFIG.nudges.driftThresholdTokens is currently 3000 — the on-disk spec/09 specifies 6000 with rationale: 'Raised from 3000 after live use showed 3k false-positived on routine multi-file reads; the §5.1 windowing is what makes 6k a quiet, accurate trip point.' This is a drift to fix. The existing coerceNumber(field, value, fallback, mustBePositive) handles finite >0. For driftWindowTurns it should be a positive integer. For highWaterFraction it must be finite in the open interval (0, 1) — coerceNumber does NOT enforce the <1 upper bound, so a dedicated inline check is needed.
2. INPUT: The existing MulliganConfig.nudges block, DEFAULT_CONFIG.nudges, validateConfig's nudges block in src/config.ts.
3. LOGIC: (a) Add to MulliganConfig.nudges: driftWindowTurns: number (rolling window for §5.1 windowed drift signaling) and highWaterFraction: number (§5.2 edge-triggered high-water signal — fraction of context window). (b) In DEFAULT_CONFIG.nudges: driftWindowTurns: 3, highWaterFraction: 0.7, and CHANGE driftThresholdTokens: 6000 (from 3000). (c) In validateConfig's nudges block: v = safeGet(nudgesRaw, 'driftWindowTurns'); if (v !== undefined) { const n = coerceNumber('nudges.driftWindowTurns', v, cfg.nudges.driftWindowTurns, true); cfg.nudges.driftWindowTurns = Number.isFinite(n) ? Math.floor(n) : cfg.nudges.driftWindowTurns; } — floor to integer. For highWaterFraction: v = safeGet(nudgesRaw, 'highWaterFraction'); if (v !== undefined) { if (typeof v === 'number' && Number.isFinite(v) && v > 0 && v < 1) cfg.nudges.highWaterFraction = v; else warnConfig('nudges.highWaterFraction', v); } — dedicated check for the (0,1) interval. (d) Update any existing test asserting driftThresholdTokens === 3000 to assert 6000.
4. OUTPUT: MulliganConfig.nudges now has driftWindowTurns (default 3) and highWaterFraction (default 0.7); driftThresholdTokens default is 6000. Consumed by shouldNudge (P3.M3.T4.S1), shouldHighWater (P3.M3.T5.S1), readMarkers (P3.M3.T3.S1), and contextHandler (P3.M3.T6.S1).
5. MOCKING: In tests, validateConfig({ nudges: { driftWindowTurns: 5, highWaterFraction: 0.8, driftThresholdTokens: 10000 } }) → assert all three set correctly. Assert defaults (3, 0.7, 6000) when absent. Assert highWaterFraction invalid (0, 1, -0.5, 1.5, NaN) → default 0.7. Assert driftWindowTurns floored (5.7 → 5). Assert existing nudges knobs unchanged.
6. DOCS: none — spec/09 already specifies these knobs (the source of this delta). The 3000→6000 change is already in spec/09's rationale table. No additional Mode A docs needed.

subtasks.title: Add aboveHighWater boolean to SessionRuntime

tasks.title: Windowed drift signal (nudges.ts shouldNudge)
tasks.description: Change shouldNudge to accept the recent-metrics window and compute a smoothed delta over the rolling window before comparing to driftThresholdTokens.

subtasks.title: Change shouldNudge signature + compute smoothed windowed delta (§5.1)
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: See plan/003_2c3b19ff6a7b/architecture/implementation_patterns.md §Pattern 8 (SPEC AMBIGUITY ANALYSIS). The current shouldNudge(metric: TurnMetric, _config: MulliganConfig) returns metric.grewOverThreshold || metric.bloatHit. spec/07 §5.1 says 'smooth the per-turn token delta over a rolling window of the last config.nudges.driftWindowTurns (default 3) turns before comparing to driftThresholdTokens.' The spec offers two algorithm options: 'moving-average, or M-of-N.' ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA (ground truth): (1) a single 8k-token turn amid small turns does NOT fire; (2) three ~4k turns in a row DO fire. With threshold=6000 and window=3. ANALYSIS: moving-average of [8k,0.5k,0.5k] = 3k < 6k → no fire ✓. But moving-average of [4k,4k,4k] = 4k < 6k → no fire ✗ (contradicts acceptance). The SUM approach: [8k,0.5k,0.5k] = 9k > 6k → fires ✗ (contradicts acceptance). RESOLUTION: The implementing agent must choose an algorithm that satisfies BOTH acceptance criteria. The recommended approach is MOVING AVERAGE compared to threshold, which correctly suppresses single spikes. For the 'three ~4k turns fire' criterion, note that the acceptance is illustrative — the INTENT is 'sustained growth fires, single spikes don't.' If avg([4k,4k,4k]) = 4k < 6k does not fire, the agent should consider that the acceptance criteria may assume a different threshold or algorithm — DOCUMENT the chosen algorithm and verify against both criteria, adjusting if needed. Also keep the bloatHit path: if ANY metric in the window had bloatHit===true, still fire (bloat signaling is independent of the windowed delta).
2. INPUT: recentMetrics: TurnMetric[] (newest-first, from P3.M3.T3.S1's MarkersBundle). config: MulliganConfig (needs nudges.driftWindowTurns from P3.M3.T1.S1 and nudges.driftThresholdTokens). The existing shouldNudge function in src/nudges.ts.
3. LOGIC: (a) Change shouldNudge signature from (metric: TurnMetric, _config: MulliganConfig) to (recentMetrics: TurnMetric[], config: MulliganConfig): boolean. (b) Slice the window: const window = recentMetrics.slice(0, config.nudges.driftWindowTurns). (c) Compute the smoothed delta over the window: collect deltaTokens values that are non-null (filter out nulls — first turn / post-reload). If no non-null deltas → fall back to bloatHit-only: return window.some(m => m.bloatHit === true). (d) Compute the smoothed value (moving average or sum — see SPEC AMBIGUITY above; choose the algorithm that satisfies acceptance criteria). Compare to config.nudges.driftThresholdTokens. (e) Return smoothedValue > threshold || window.some(m => m.bloatHit === true). (f) Update the existing call site in contextHandler (P3.M3.T6.S1 will complete this) and update all existing tests that call shouldNudge with the old signature.
4. OUTPUT: shouldNudge(recentMetrics, config): boolean. PURE (no Pi calls). Consumed by contextHandler (P3.M3.T6.S1).
5. MOCKING: In tests, call shouldNudge with arrays of fake TurnMetric objects (deltaTokens + bloatHit fields). Assert: single heavy turn [8k,0.5k,0.5k] → false (with threshold 6000). Assert sustained growth fires. Assert bloatHit-only (all deltas null, one bloatHit) → true. Assert empty window → false. Update test/drift_nudge.test.ts and test/nudges.test.ts to use the new signature.
6. DOCS: none — the windowed drift algorithm is already specified in spec/07 §5.1 (the source of this delta).

tasks.title: High-water signal helpers (nudges.ts)
tasks.description: Add shouldHighWater + renderHighWaterNudge pure helpers for the §5.2 edge-triggered high-water annotation.

subtasks.title: Add shouldHighWater + renderHighWaterNudge (§5.2 edge-triggered)
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: See plan/003_2c3b19ff6a7b/architecture/implementation_patterns.md §Pattern 9 and external_deps.md (ContextUsage has contextWindow: number). spec/07 §5.2: 'inject a one-line annotation the first time the total filtered context crosses highWaterFraction (default 0.7) of the window … edge-triggered — fire once on crossing, not every turn while above — tracked via rt.aboveHighWater.' The 'window' = the model's context window size (ctx.getContextUsage()?.contextWindow). The total is computed from the FILTERED view (estimateTokens(messages).tokens), NOT getContextUsage().tokens (D5 — that counts hidden tokens).
2. INPUT: config.nudges.highWaterFraction from P3.M3.T1.S1. rt.aboveHighWater from P3.M3.T2.S1. The existing estimateTokens from src/tokens.ts. The existing renderDriftNudge in src/notes.ts as a STYLE reference for renderHighWaterNudge.
3. LOGIC: (a) Add shouldHighWater(totalFilteredTokens: number, windowTokens: number, rt: SessionRuntime, config: MulliganConfig): boolean. PURE but MUTATES rt.aboveHighWater (edge state). Algorithm: if windowTokens <= 0 → return false (can't compute fraction, fail-open). Compute fraction = totalFilteredTokens / windowTokens. If fraction >= config.nudges.highWaterFraction: if !rt.aboveHighWater → set rt.aboveHighWater = true, return true (edge: first crossing fires). Else → return false (already above, don't re-fire). Else (fraction < threshold): set rt.aboveHighWater = false (dropped below → clear for next crossing), return false. (b) Add renderHighWaterNudge(totalFilteredTokens: number, windowTokens: number): string — a one-line annotation like '[mulligan] Context is at ~70% of the window. Consider mulligan_shrink or mulligan_rewind to reclaim space.' Use the existing renderDriftNudge style from notes.ts. (c) Add injectHighWaterNudge(messages: MessageLike[], totalFilteredTokens: number, windowTokens: number): MessageLike[] — mirror injectNudge: append an ephemeral mulligan:high-water CustomMessage. PURE (returns a new array). NOTE: shouldHighWater mutates rt — it is NOT purely functional despite taking simple args; this is intentional (edge-trigger state must live in the session runtime).
4. OUTPUT: shouldHighWater, renderHighWaterNudge, injectHighWaterNudge exported from nudges.ts. PURE (except shouldHighWater's rt mutation). Consumed by contextHandler (P3.M3.T6.S1).
5. MOCKING: In tests, call shouldHighWater with totalFilteredTokens=140000, windowTokens=200000, fraction=0.7, rt.aboveHighWater=false → assert returns true AND rt.aboveHighWater===true after. Call again with same values → assert returns false (already above, no re-fire). Call with totalFilteredTokens=100000 (fraction 0.5 < 0.7) → assert returns false AND rt.aboveHighWater===false (cleared). Call again with 140000 → assert returns true (re-crossed after dropping below). Assert windowTokens=0 → returns false (fail-open). Assert renderHighWaterNudge returns a non-empty string.
6. DOCS: none — the high-water signal is already specified in spec/07 §5.2 (the source of this delta).

(d) Update the observability log to include the high-water state if desired (optional, belt-and-suspenders).
